messages:
emma (support): FYI customer 'LearnLoop' reporting p99 for text-generation jumped from ~160ms -> ~1.2s since last night's infra deploy. they opened a support ticket, attaching traces.
jon (oncall): Ack. Which pool/region?
emma (support): eu-west-1 hosted pool. Affects ~12% of their requests, mostly long-context chat flows. They say it started around 02:10 UTC.
priya (infra): That aligns with the scheduled CUDA/driver rollout we ran 02:00-02:40 across eu-west-1. Driver package moved from 525.40 -> 525.85 + CUDA deps.
alex (sre): Any kernel updates paired with that window?
priya (infra): No kernel change. Just driver and firmware bump on GPU fleet nodes in pool-hosted-eu1-a/b. deploy-bot: rollout eu-west-1/gpu-driver/525.85 completed 02:39 UTC.
mason (cust-succ): Customer's logs show many requests with backend timings: `x-rrt: 1100ms`, `x-infer-time: 980ms`. They attached a sample curl: `curl -s -D- -o /dev/null "https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"model":"redwood-1-small","input":"..."}'`
jon (oncall): Can someone repro from inside the cluster? I'll spin a quick load against an affected node.
priya (infra): I'm pulling dmesg and iostat from one of the flagged nodes. Preliminary: elevated block device latency on nvme0n1 during high-concurrency inference. iostat shows avg await climb from 1.5ms -> 15ms around 02:10.
alex (sre): That smells like IO interference between driver/firmware change and the host NVMe driver. Any NVRM Xid errors in dmesg?
priya (infra): Found repeated `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, pid 1234` around 02:12 and then large pauses logged by the NVMe controller: `nvme0: I/O 512 queued, nvme_io_timeout`.
jon (oncall): Repro steps from a node: run a synthetic inference load with same batch/burst. I'm getting p99 ~1.1s locally on the node when background fio runs random-read 4k -m 4k -q 32. Without fio, p99 ~140ms.
emma (support): Customer says they do not see heavy block IO on their workload, but our shared infra might be.
priya (infra): Hypothesis: new driver/firmware changes changed DMA patterns -> more host-side NVMe queue pressure under our inference kernel. Could be interaction with PCIe peer-to-peer or NVMe driver.
jon (oncall): Immediate mitigations we can try: 1) drain affected nodes from pool and failover traffic to standby nodes still on 525.40, 2) throttle background IO (snapshot jobs), 3) temporarily route heavy-chat customers to dedicated pool.
alex (sre): Also we can revert the driver on a small canary set to confirm.
priya (infra): I'm gating a rollback plan. Rolling back drivers on 3 nodes in eu1-a now to 525.40 and taking them back into rotation for quick A/B.
deploy-bot: rollback-start eu-west-1/gpu-driver -> 525.40 at 03:01 UTC (user: priya)
jon (oncall): After taking one node back to 525.40 and running the same synthetic load, p99 falls back to ~150ms. Confirmed regression introduced by 525.85 rollout.
mason (cust-succ): I informed LearnLoop: we have a targeted rollback in progress and will route their traffic to unaffected nodes. Offering provisional credits for the window.
priya (infra): Expanding rollback to remaining eu-west-1 nodes. ETA 20m. Opening vendor ticket with NVIDIA, attaching nvme and NVRM logs. nvidia-eng-bot: Ticket created with NVIDIA (case # NV-2026-1683).
jon (oncall): Short-term cluster-level mitigations: 1) pause noncritical background IO (backups/fio snapshots) in eu-west-1, 2) reduce default inference batch size from 8 -> 4 for hosted-eu1 to lower per-request IO spikes, 3) increase filesystem writeback throttling (sysctl vm.dirty_ratio -> 5) on nodes until rollback completes.
priya (infra): Implementing sysctl change now and pausing snapshots via orchestration.
emma (support): Customer update: LearnLoop responded :relieved: thanks, they see improved latency on their end when we moved their traffic.
alex (sre): Postmortem actions we should track: - fully rollback to 525.40 in eu-west-1 until vendor confirms fix - run targeted stress tests (high concurrency + fio rw mix) on canary nodes before any future driver rollouts - add nvme queue-depth and kernel IO metrics to model-level dashboards - expose a routing flag to auto-fail customers to dedicated pools on infra regressions
mason (cust-succ): I'll draft the customer-facing note and remediation timeline.
priya (infra): Logging follow-ups: saved full `dmesg`, `nvme-cli` smart logs, and `iostat -x 1 300` traces to S3 at s3://redwood-incidents/3502109876/; linked in the ticket.
jon (oncall): Owner: priya (infra) for rollback and vendor comms. Alex to own postmortem and dashboards. Emma/mason to handle customer comms and credits.
priya (infra): Rollback completed for eu-west-1 at 03:33 UTC. Monitoring: p99 trending back to baseline across pools.
emma (support): LearnLoop confirms p99 back to ~170ms. Closing loop with them, will keep monitoring for 24h.
alex (sre): Great work. We'll keep the incident open until vendor provides root cause. Created incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/3502109876 (private).
jon (oncall): Adding follow-up tasks to our runbook: add driver-rollout stress gating and explicit nvme health checks.
emma (support): Thanks team :heart:
